issues.description: Command names break the established singular quickmark-/bookmark- naming convention.
issues.detail: Sibling commands use singular hyphenated form (quickmark-save, quickmark-add, bookmark-add, bookmark-load), but the new commands register as quickmarks_reload/bookmarks_reload (plural). The feature-file BDD steps also use the plural form. This breaks the implicit naming contract callers rely on for discoverability. Rename to quickmark-reload / bookmark-reload.

issues.description: reload() clears state before parsing, leaving the manager half-populated on parse failure.
issues.detail: The contract should be: postcondition leaves marks matching disk, OR raises and leaves prior state untouched. Current code clears marks first then parses; if _parse_line raises (InvalidUrlError, etc.), the manager is left half-populated with changed already emitted. Parse-then-swap, or document the partial-failure contract and unsaved-discard behavior in the docstring.

issues.description: Routing __init__ through reload() emits changed during construction, altering the signal contract.
issues.detail: Previously the constructor populated marks without emitting changed; now __init__ calls reload() which fires changed.emit(). Any subscriber connected at construction, or future code assuming changed means a post-init mutation, will see a spurious initial event. The signal's implicit contract — fired on user-visible mutation — is weakened.

issues.description: New BDD scenarios use bare 'Scenario:' with no descriptive name.
issues.detail: Every other scenario in this feature file has a descriptive name (e.g. 'Saving a quickmark'). The two new ones are unnamed, breaking the file's voice and hurting traceability. Name them, e.g. 'Reloading bookmarks from disk'. Cheap fix.

issues.description: Unit test for reload() under-covers the contract: only verifies replacement of one entry.
issues.detail: test_reload only proves one entry can be swapped for another. The interesting postconditions — entries removed from disk disappear, added entries appear, ordering reflects disk — are not asserted. Add a multi-entry test with disjoint before/after sets, and assert pre-reload state to catch __init__ regressions.

issues.description: reload() docstring lacks pre/postconditions and leaks subtype language.
issues.detail: The method lives on UrlMarkManager (supertype) but the docstring says 'Reload quickmarks/bookmarks from disk'. State the supertype contract: 'Discard current marks and repopulate from the backing file; emits changed on completion; discards unsaved in-memory state.' Subtypes inherit it unchanged.

synthesis.summary: The patch adds a useful reload operation with a clean refactor folding __init__'s parse loop into a reusable reload() method — that shape lands. However, the panel agrees on three substantive issues: the new command names (quickmarks_reload/bookmarks_reload) break the established singular quickmark-/bookmark- convention used by every sibling command; reload() clears state before parsing, leaving the manager half-populated if parsing raises; and routing __init__ through reload() now emits changed during construction, weakening the signal's contract. Secondary issues: unnamed BDD scenarios, thin unit-test coverage of reload's actual contract, and a docstring that omits pre/postconditions. NEEDS-WORK before landing.
